---
title: "PC1/PC2 vs Cell Volume"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Paths relative to this Rmd's location (Adriana_analysis/scripts/)
project_dir <- ".."
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_functions.rda"))

paths       <- setup_project_paths(project_dir)
tables_dir  <- paths$tables_dir
figures_dir <- paths$figures_dir
output_dir  <- paths$output_dir
```

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# Shared colour palette for dissertation figures
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_colours.rda"))
```

```{r load-pca-samples}
# Sample-level PCA scores (93 samples), joined against mean cell
# volume per sample. This is the direct validation that PC1 and PC2
# mean what scripts 03/06/09 assume they mean - those scripts only
# ever compute cor_PC1_vol / cor_PC2_vol as a subtitle number, with
# no standalone figure showing the relationship. This script produces
# that figure.
pca_samples <- read_tsv(file.path(tables_dir, "PCA_samples_AC.txt"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_cell_volume))

pc_vol_cor <- pca_samples %>%
  summarise(
    cor_PC1_vol = cor(PC1, mean_cell_volume, method = "spearman"),
    cor_PC2_vol = cor(PC2, mean_cell_volume, method = "spearman")
  )

cat("PC1 vs cell volume (Spearman r):", round(pc_vol_cor$cor_PC1_vol, 3), "\n")
cat("PC2 vs cell volume (Spearman r):", round(pc_vol_cor$cor_PC2_vol, 3), "\n")
cat("n samples:", nrow(pca_samples), "\n")
```

```{r plot-pc1-vs-volume}
p_pc1_vol <- ggplot(pca_samples, aes(x = mean_cell_volume, y = PC1)) +
  geom_point(color = project_colours[["purple"]], alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PC1 sample score against measured cell volume",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "n = ", nrow(pca_samples), " samples | ",
      "Spearman r = ", round(pc_vol_cor$cor_PC1_vol, 3)
    ),
    x = "Mean cell volume (fL)",
    y = "PC1 sample score"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

print(p_pc1_vol)
```

```{r plot-pc2-vs-volume}
p_pc2_vol <- ggplot(pca_samples, aes(x = mean_cell_volume, y = PC2)) +
  geom_point(color = project_colours[["blue"]], alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PC2 sample score against measured cell volume",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "n = ", nrow(pca_samples), " samples | ",
      "Spearman r = ", round(pc_vol_cor$cor_PC2_vol, 3)
    ),
    x = "Mean cell volume (fL)",
    y = "PC2 sample score"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

print(p_pc2_vol)
```

```{r combined-panel}
# Side-by-side panel is the version for the dissertation - shows PC1
# and PC2 have opposite relationships with volume in one figure,
# which is the actual point (PC2 tracks size, PC1 does not).
p_combined <- p_pc1_vol + p_pc2_vol +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)

print(p_combined)
```

```{r save-outputs}
write_tsv(pc_vol_cor, file.path(output_dir, "pc_vs_cell_volume_correlations.txt"))

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "figure_pc1_vs_cell_volume.png"),
       plot = p_pc1_vol, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "figure_pc2_vs_cell_volume.png"),
       plot = p_pc2_vol, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "figure_pc1_pc2_vs_cell_volume_combined.png"),
       plot = p_combined, width = 11, height = 5, dpi = 300)

cat("Done - results saved to output_tables/ and figures/\n")
```
